thread.title: Tech Today: Can Tesla Keep It Up? Dell Going Public, Facebook's Instagram Numbers

author: Barron's
title: Tech Today: Can Tesla Keep It Up? Dell Going Public, Facebook's Instagram Numbers
text:
Here are some things going on today in the world of tech :
Can Tesla Keep It Up? Shares of Tesla ( TSLA ) are up $18.27, or 5%, to $361.22, after the company this morning said it reached its goal of making 5,000 units per week of its Model 3 sedan in the quarter at the last possible moment, producing 5,031 Model 3s during the last seven days of the quarter.
Total production of all Tesla vehicles in the quarter of 53,339 was more than most on the Street had been expecting. The company said it expects to reach 6,000 units made per week by late July. It also repeated a claim Tesla will reach positive GAAP net income and cash flow in Q3 and Q4 of this year.
Chief Executive Elon Musk had actually tweeted the news Sunday evening .
7000 cars, 7 days ♥️ Tesla Team ♥️
- Elon Musk (@elonmusk)
July 1, 2018
Some differing reactions to this, this morning. Trip Chowdhry with Global Equities Research , who had been consistently bullish about the company's production abilities, writes today that "betting against TSLA is not only insane, but total stupidity."
But Rajvindra Gill of Needham & Co . raises a question many will have today: Is it sustainable?
"What's uncertain, however, is can the company sustain this level of production for more than a week and at what cost?"
He notes in particular "Reports indicating Panasonic has been capacity constrained on the batteries" as something that "could slow production rates."
"Given the sheer number of cells (4k), the necessity to have yields on the battery packs in the mid-90s, and the aggressive timeline, production challenges could resume," he writes.
Dell Going Public CNBC Personal-computer and enterprise-tech conglomeration Dell is ready to go public again, on the New York Stock Exchange , announcing this morning that the company will exchange its common shares for in return for shares of the tracking stock of its ownership in VMware ( VMW ), the Dell Technologies Class V ( DVMT ),
The offer includes $109 in cash per share offered to DVMT holders, if they so choose, which would be a 29% premium to the stock price. DVMT shares have been on a tear in recent weeks, rising about 28% since the beginning of May as people like Carl Icahn bet on the shares .
The stock is up $6.04, or 7%, to $90.62, this morning.
Chairman and CEO Michael Dell will continue to own the majority of Dell stock. Speaking on CNBC a short while ago, Dell said the board decided the stock swap is the best way to "simplify the capital structure" of Dell.
"There is a tech-led boom in investment that requires modern IT infrastructure, and Dell Technologies is the leading infrastructure company on the planet," said Dell. Dell said this approach to going public was simpler than other potential approaches, such as having a public offering for Dell and later converting the tracking stock into Dell stock.
Shares of VMware are up $8.12, or 5.5%, to $155.09, as the exchange offer is causing bulls such as Shebly Seyrafi of FBN Securities to breathe a sigh of relief.
The stock swap "avoids the speculated reverse merger scenario wherein VMW would acquire Dell, which would have saddled VMW with more debt and been more disruptive to VMW's business," he notes.
VMware is going to pay an $11 billion cash dividend, the majority of its $12.6 billion in cash on the balance sheet to its shareholders, of which the majority is getting paid to Dell, since Dell owns 81% of VMware.
Seyrafi notes that will change VMware from a net cash position of $8.3 billion negative $2.60 billion, "but we estimate that VMW will have a F2019 FCF of $3.34B, so we expect VMW to go back to a positive net cash position in late F2019."
Facebook's Instagram'Gap' Shares of Facebook ( FB ) are up 13 cents to $194.45, after Wells Fargo 's Ken Sena this morning raised his price target on the shares to $250 from $230, and reiterated his Outperform rating, predicting that the company's Instagram photo sharing property will see a lift as advertisers warm to the " Stories " portion of the property.
With 400 million users, as recently disclosed by Facebook, Instagram has a "meaningful revenue opportunity," notes Sena, and the Stories part of Instagram, where people post videos, as opposed to still images, is now probably almost one third of all activity , estimates Sena.
But Stories, based on data from third party Kenshoo , writes Sena, makes up just 6% of total Instagram revenue, which means, he writes, that Instagram "monetizes" at just one quarter the rate of the rest of Instagram.
"We believe this'gap' can close quickly," writes Sena, based on his chats with advertisers and agencies. "Our forecast assumes IG Stories can reach Snapchat's current level of monetization (or $5 per DAU, up from $1 today) by 2020E, adding $4bn in incremental revenue to IG alone.
"Meanwhile, assuming IG feed can grow monetization at a 31% CAGR through 2020E (or similar FB's growth following its mobile inflection), we see over $20bn in combined revenue between the two. "
Relief for Apple Shares of Apple ( AAPL ) are up 66 cents to $185.77, after Citigroup 's Jim Suva this morning pounded the table for the shares, reiterating a Buy rating and a $200 price target, writing that with Street estimates for iPhone having been cut for months now, consensus is now in line with his own estimates. That "right-sizing" of expectations, he thinks, should offer some relief for the stock.
Lumentum's Augmented Prospects Speaking of Apple, Piper Jaffray 's Troy Jensen this morning reiterates an Overweight rating on Lumentum Holdings (LITE), calling it one of the best stocks to own in the fiber-optic component market, given it will remain the "primary supplier for Apple" for the iPhone for so-called augmented reality , the use of lasers to create effects such as the facial recognition feature in the iPhone X.
"We believe Apple will be including 3D sensing in all three iPhones this fall," writes Jensen.
"We continue to believe Apple will introduce 3D sensing in the upcoming iPad Pro launch and anticipate more Apple tablets and PCs will include this capability throughout 2019.
"We believe Apple will also introduce world facing 3D sensing capabilities in fall 2019.
"It is our belief Lumentum is qualified for Apple's upcoming launch and share of VCSELs in these phones could be as much as 70-75%, but the actual amount will be dependent on how much business II-VI will be able to supply as the likely No. 2 supplier this year."
Lumentum stock is up 55 cents, or 1%, to $58.45.
